simple.meaning: אָפֵס (ʼâphêç) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to disappear , i.e. cease.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 5 times across Genesis, Psalms, Isaiah, beginning at Genesis 47:15. Its contexts include land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָפֵס (H656).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: אָפֵס (ʼâphêç) / H656 is traced through Genesis 47:15, Genesis 47:16, Psalms 77:9, Isaiah 16:4 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: When the money was all spent in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came to Joseph, and said, “Give us bread, for why should we die in your presence? For our money fails.”

timeline.evidenceText: When the money was all spent in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came to Joseph, and said, “Give us bread, for why should we die in your presence? For our money fails.”
Joseph said, “Give me your livestock; and I will give you food for your livestock, if your money is gone.”
Has God forgotten to be gracious?

Let my outcasts dwell with you! As for Moab, be a hiding place for him from the face of the destroyer. For the extortionist is brought to nothing. Destruction ceases. The oppressors are consumed out of the land.
For the ruthless is brought to nothing, and the scoffer ceases, and all those who are alert to do evil are cut off—

definitions.usage: be clean gone (at an end, brought to nought), fail.
definitions.full: H656. aphes אָפֵס (compare מָּסַס ) verb cease, fail, come to an end : only Qal Perfect 3masculine singular; Gen 47:15-16 , (of money, כֶּסֶף ), Isa 16:4 (extortioner: || תַּם כָּלָה, ), 29:20 (terrible one: || נִכְרַת כָּלָה, ), Psa 77:9 ( חסְדּוֺ || גָּמַר ).
